zh: 佛罗里达州立大学（，简称 FSU）是美国一所公立研究型大学，其主校区位于佛罗里达州首府塔拉哈西市，占地489英亩(2.0平方公里). 它成立于1851年，是佛罗里达州最早创立的高等教育机构，也是佛罗里达州立大学系统的早期成员学校.
佛罗里达州立大学有来自全美50个州和130多个国家和地区的44,308名学生和6,700多位教职员工(2024年). 教授中有6位诺贝尔奖得主及22名美国国家科学院院士. 根据《美国新闻与世界报导》的排名，佛罗里达州立大学在2024年被列为最佳公立大学第23位，全美最佳大学第54位，全球排名约为一百多名.

佛罗里达州立大学被卡内基教学促进基金会归类为最高的「R1 : 博士类大学 - 研究活动非常活跃」. 根据 2023 年国家科学基金会的数据，佛罗里达州立大学2023年的研发（R&D）支出为4.14亿美元，在 890 所评估机构中排名第 79 位. 该大学的年度预算超过30亿美元，每年的经济影响超过155亿美元. 该大学由16个独立学院和110多个系所、研究中心和实验室所组成，提供超过360个学位和专业学位课程. 校内设有全佛州唯一的国家实验室-美国国家超强磁场实验室，它也是商业上著名的抗癌药物紫杉醇的发源地. 佛罗里达州立大学还经营著John＆Mable Ringling艺术博物馆、佛罗里达州立美术馆和全国最大的大学综合博物馆.
FSU的运动代表队以其塞米诺尔人的绰号而闻名，是大西洋沿岸联盟会员. 在他们超过一百年的历史中，佛罗里达州立大学的运动代表队共赢得了20个全国运动冠军，其运动员共赢得了78个NCAA个人全国冠军.

佛罗里达州立大学所在的城市塔拉哈西是佛罗里达州的首府, 距离墨西哥湾约40公里. 佛罗里达州立大学总校园共超过1,600英亩（6平方公里），其中塔拉哈西市主校区占地489英亩（2.0平方公里），总建筑物面积超过14,800,000平方英尺（1,375,000平方米）. 主校区西边是体育场大道，北边是田纳西大街（美国90号公路），东边是马科姆街，南边是盖恩斯街. Westcott 大楼位于 College Avenue 和 S. Copeland Street 的交汇处，可能是学校最突出的建筑. Westcott 位于佛罗里达州最古老的高等教育场所，是 Ruby Diamond Auditorium 的所在地，也是该大学的首要表演场所. 校园的原始图书馆 Dodd Hall 在美国建筑师协会佛罗里达州建筑名单上排名第10位. 此外，佛罗里达州立大学在巴拿马市还有一个分校区.
en: Florida State University (FSU or Florida State) is a public research university in Tallahassee, Florida, United States. It is a senior member of the State University System of Florida and a preeminent university in the state. Chartered in 1851, it is located on Florida's oldest continuous site of higher education.

Florida State University maintains 17 colleges, as well as 58 centers, facilities, labs, institutes, and professional training programs. In 2024, the university enrolled 44,308 students from all 50 states and 130 countries. Florida State is home to Florida's only national laboratory, the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, and was instrumental in the commercial development of the anti-cancer drug Taxol. Florida State University also operates the John & Mable Ringling Museum of Art, the State Art Museum of Florida and one of the nation's largest museum/university complexes. The university is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools (SACSCOC).

The university is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research spending and doctorate production". Per 2023 National Science Foundation data the university had research and development (R&D) expenditures of $414.46 million and ranked 79th out of 890 evaluated institutions. The university has an annual budget of $3 billion and an annual estimated economic impact of $15.5 billion.

Florida State has a collaborative relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida and is allowed to use the name Seminoles and certain imagery. FSU's intercollegiate sports teams, known by their "Florida State Seminoles" nickname, compete in National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I and the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC). Florida State's varsity teams have won 19 all-time national athletic championships in nine sports.

Florida State University is traceable to a plan set by the 1823 U.S. Congress to create a higher education system. The 1838 Florida Constitution codified the primary system by providing for land allocated for the schools. In 1845 Congress passed the law admitting Florida as the 27th state. In a supplementary act to the law granting admission, Congress authorized two townships to host seminaries, one east and one west of the Suwannee River. In 1851, the Florida Legislature authorized the seminaries to be awarded to the two towns offering the best school support. The legislature declared the first purpose of these institutions was to train male and female teachers in all subjects generally taught at public schools, then to educate the public in agriculture, science, law and citizenship. While the East Seminary was settled in Ocala in 1853, the West Seminary state institution opportunity created a contentious fight between the towns of Quincy, Marianna, and Tallahassee. Quincy dropped out of the competition in the following years, while Marianna and Tallahassee refused to yield. Failing to resolve the impasse, the conflict was returned to the governor and legislature for resolution. In 1854, as an incentive to the state, Tallahassee re-established an old school for boys, now called the Florida Institute, and combined the school with land and buildings. The legislature finally awarded Tallahassee with the West Seminary in 1856. The governor signed the law on January 1, 1857. In October 1858 the school was made coeducational by incorporating the Female Institute, which was located nearby. The West Florida Seminary was located on the former Florida Institute property. The area, slightly west of the state Capitol, was formerly and ominously known as Gallows Hill, a place for public executions in early Tallahassee.
